newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MMS proposes change in oil royalty accounting.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MMS proposes change in oil royalty accounting.

text.p: Pressured to ensure that companies do not undervalue oil produced on federal land, the Minerals Management Service proposed Friday to limit the use of gross proceeds as the basis for calculating royalties.

"The intent of the proposed rule is to reduce reliance on posted prices for royalty valuation, reflect true market value, provide certainty to all involved, and provide maximum flexibility to adapt to changing market conditions," said MMS Director Cynthia Quarterman.

Under the proposal, for the large portion of production sold under exchange agreements or sold to affiliates, MMS would assess royalties based on resale prices or the monthly average of NYMEX futures prices or Alaska North Slope crude prices, with adjustments for location and quality.
For arm's length sales--sales tied to no other deals-- MMS would continue to assess royalties based on gross proceeds.
MMS said the proposal would be open for comment for 60 days after it was officially published.

The agency was repeatedly criticized last year for failing to collect all that it was owed by oil companies in California and several other states, because it used a system linked to companies' posted prices, which were lower than market prices.
